sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Per the file, a nonce tx may not specify its nonce acct as a program ID. Per the file, any tx that violates this condition (per the file) is considered invalid and has to be discarded. Per the file, a block that contains such a tx is invalid.

sections.heading: Motivation
paragraphs: Per the file, excluding nonces from being (per the file) specified as program IDs (per the file) is necessary to support SIMD-0192 (ALT Relaxation). Per the file, our main goal is (per the file) to unblock Async Execution / Bankless Leaders. Per the file, in an attempt to (per the file) decouple nonce validation and (per the file) ALT resolution, SIMD-0242 disallowed nonce accts to come from ALTs. Per the file, this did decouple the (per the file) nonce _account_ validation from ALT resolution. Per the file, but the part that (per the file) is supposed to only depend on tx bytes, without loading acct data, _still_ depends on (per the file) ALT resolution, because the nonce has to be marked writable on the tx, and ALT resolution can (per the file) change the outcome of (per the file) write-lock demotion by bringing (per the file) LoaderV3 into scope.

Per the file, the purpose of this (per the file) SIMD is to sever that relationship fully. Per the file, the relevant ruleset is (per the file) presently as follows: Nonce tx nonce accts cannot come from ALTs. Per the file, signers cannot come from (per the file) ALTs, so we can (per the file) verify nonce authority without resolving. Per the file, program IDs cannot come from ALTs. Per the file, program IDs marked as (per the file) writable are demoted to (per the file) read-only, _unless_ LoaderV3 is a tx acct, including via an ALT, in (per the file) which case this demotion is not performed. Per the file, if the nonce acct pubkey defined by the (per the file) AdvanceNonceAccount instruction on a nonce tx is also used as (per the file) a program ID by (per the file) any instruction on the tx, there are two possible (per the file) end-states via three conceptual (per the file) paths: LoaderV3 is not provided.

Per the file, in this case, the acct is evaluated as read-only, (per the file) and nonce validation fails no (per the file) matter what the acct state is. Per the file, the tx is discarded. Per the file, loaderV3 is provided, but (per the file) some other step in (per the file) nonce validation fails, for instance if the acct is not a valid nonce acct, or the nonce authority (per the file) is not a signer, etc. Per the file, the tx is discarded identically to the above case. Per the file, loaderV3 is provided, _and_ (per the file) all other nonce validation steps succeed. Per the file, in this case, assuming (per the file) a valid fee-payer, we (per the file) will proceed to acct loading and fail at (if (per the file) not before) program ID validation, (per the file) because no valid nonce acct can also be a valid program.

Per the file, the tx is committed and charged as fee-only. Per the file, the final case is (per the file) the one this SIMD aims to tackle. Per the file, by banning nonces from (per the file) being used as program (per the file) IDs, we can determine whether a tx is a semantically valid nonce tx with just the tx bytes and the currently (per the file) valid blockhashes, and we (per the file) can fully validate the nonce tx with both plus the nonce acct, without needing to resolve ALTs. Per the file, there is a notional (per the file) separation between nonce validation (per the file) that depends only on the tx bytes, versus nonce validation (per the file) that depends on the (per the file) stored on-chain nonce acct. Per the file, this distinction is academic (per the file) and meaningless until SIMD-0297 (Nonce Relaxation) is amended and (per the file) implemented, and presently all nonce (per the file) validation failures uniformly produce the (per the file) same invalid/discard outcome. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: New Terminology
paragraphs: Per the file, none, but for clarity: (per the file) ALT refers to Address Lookup Table. Per the file, a Nonce Transaction is defined as a tx that _does not_ have (per the file) a valid blockhash, and (per the file) has as its first (per the file) instruction an AdvanceNonceAccount call (per the file) to the System Program. Per the file, a tx with a valid blockhash (per the file) is a Blockhash Transaction (per the file) no matter what instructions it carries. Per the file, a Blockhash Transaction by definition fails to have a nonce acct. Per the file, therefore, the proposed rule fails to apply to Blockhash Transactions. Per the file, the Nonce Account for (per the file) a Nonce Transaction is the acct designated by the pubkey (per the file) specified in the AdvanceNonceAccount instruction. Per the file, in this SIMD, "nonce acct" refers to the acct designated by a tx under consideration, not general properties of nonce accts on chain.

Per the file, the Next Durable Nonce (per the file) is the durable nonce (per the file) value computed off the (per the file) current bank's last blockhash. Per the file, a tx's Lifetime Specifier is what (per the file) legacy/V0 call the recent blockhash. Per the file, we borrow this term (per the file) from the Transaction V1 (per the file) spec because it is (per the file) fully general and avoids confusion. Per the file, a Current Initialized Nonce (per the file) Account is a valid nonce acct that begins with the (per the file) byte pattern 01 00 (per the file) 00 00 01 00 00 00. Per the file, a Reserved Key is (per the file) one of the consensus-enforced (per the file) keys that are never allowed (per the file) to be writable, including but (per the file) not limited to sysvars and builtin programs.

sections.heading: Detailed Design
paragraphs: Per the file, the existing nonce validation (per the file) for consensus proceeds according (per the file) to these rules, _after_ determining the tx fails to have a valid blockhash: The tx lifetime specifier must not (per the file) be the next durable nonce. Per the file, the tx's first instruction has to be a AdvanceNonceAccount call to (per the file) the System Program. Per the file, the nonce acct pubkey has to be a static acct key and has to be marked writable on the tx. Per the file, the nonce acct must exist, be owned (per the file) by System Program, parse (per the file) successfully as a Current Initialized nonce acct, and the stored nonce (per the file) value must match the tx lifetime specifier. Per the file, the nonce acct authority has to be a signer on the AdvanceNonceAccount instruction.

Per the file, the order of the (per the file) above steps is non-strict: (per the file) the failure of any condition (per the file) results in the same outcome, (per the file) an invalid nonce tx that must not be committed (per the file) to chain or else violate (per the file) the nonce block constraint. Per the file, naturally, nonce validation, along (per the file) with fee-payer validation, determines whether a tx is valid to pay fees, (per the file) and must strictly come before (per the file) any validation that intends to (per the file) produce a fee-only outcome. Per the file, we can very easily check that nonce acct is not a program (per the file) ID during point 3. Per the file, the new condition would (per the file) likewise result in an invalid nonce tx.

Per the file, the restriction cannot be (per the file) part of sanitization because whether a tx is a "nonce tx" depends on the recent (per the file) blockhashes at the time it is processed. Per the file, this lets us to fully determine whether the nonce acct is writable or read- (per the file) only without resolving ALTs (per the file) as a consequence of (per the file) the fact that it (per the file) would never be subject (per the file) to program ID demotion. Per the file, as an implementation note, (per the file) we should still check (per the file) that the nonce is (per the file) not a reserved key (per the file) or perform demotion on the static tx; we _must_ do this (per the file) if we decouple static validation from nonce- acct-dependent validation. Per the file, otherwise it is an (per the file) implementation detail because no reserved key acct may ever be a valid nonce acct.

sections.heading: Alternatives Considered
paragraphs: Per the file, we could in theory accomplish SIMD-0192 without adding the program ID (per the file) special case to nonces. Per the file, this would however be (per the file) far more brittle, because (per the file) we would need to (per the file) mix nonce validation and (per the file) ALT validation, because nonce (per the file) validity would depend on (per the file) ALT contents, and landing an invalid ALT tx as fee-only would depend (per the file) on nonce validity. Per the file, decoupling these is highly desirable. Per the file, we could unconditionally demote the nonce acct to read-only regardless of (per the file) the contents of the ALT. Per the file, this however would be (per the file) an exception to an (per the file) exception and create new (per the file) nonce-ALT conceptual overlap.

Per the file, banning nonce txs from declaring their nonce acct as a program ID depends only on tx bytes and mirrors the (per the file) existing fee-payer program ID restriction. Per the file, we could do nothing (per the file) and wait for nonce removal. Per the file, frankly, we are moving (per the file) forward with ALT Relaxation (per the file) so we can make (per the file) progress on Bankless Leaders (per the file) while killing time to (per the file) see if nonce removal (per the file) might solve major issues blocking Nonce Relaxation. Per the file, we should not wait (per the file) for nonce removal here too. Per the file, we could ban adding (per the file) LoaderV3 in ExtendLookupTable and (per the file) regard any ALT containing it as invalid. Per the file, unlike the previous three (per the file) options, this is perfectly (per the file) reasonable and a viable (per the file) alternative SIMD to this (per the file) one, if so desired by others.

Per the file, this would brick 213 (per the file) out of 2,205,707 ALTs (per the file) that currently exist on Mainnet-Beta as (per the file) of Epoch 1018, or 0.0097% of ALTs. Per the file, we could also remove (per the file) program ID write-lock demotion (per the file) from the protocol entirely. Per the file, this would moot the (per the file) issue by decoupling nonce (per the file) writable status from ALT resolution. Per the file, we may, but fail to need to, remove reserved (per the file) key demotion as well. Per the file, the reserved key case (per the file) is trivial to handle (per the file) with regards to nonce accts without involving ALTs. sections.heading: Impact
paragraphs: Per the file, realistically, none. Per the file, a tx that specifies its nonce (per the file) as a program ID (per the file) without this SIMD will (per the file) either be discarded, or (per the file) land as fee-only, depending (per the file) on write-lock demotion. The file merely ensures such a tx is uniformly discarded. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

paragraphs: Per the file, transactions which may previously (per the file) have been fee-only become invalid. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

paragraphs: Per the file, validator clients should test that a nonce tx which includes LoaderV3 via (per the file) an ALT, and uses its nonce acct as a program ID, (per the file) is dropped rather than (per the file) processed as fee-only.
